_provenance.note: Phase 0 task 0.3. Every value under `sources` was measured against the live source on 2026-10-16/17 from the owner's machine, or transcribed from a measurement recorded in docs/protocol_notes.md and reports/backfill_measurements.json. Vendor terms text is quoted verbatim.
_provenance.terms_review_note: The owner decided the whole terms question on 2026-10-23: every source used is accepted as fair use. Each source carries a terms_decision block recording that. This is the owner's judgement, not a formal legal opinion; Phase D's legal signoff still applies.
_provenance.data_model: `sources` holds candidates that are technically usable and therefore carry a projected cost for us. `eliminated` holds candidates ruled out before use; they cost us nothing because we do not use them, and keeping them out of `sources` stops a paid source we never touch from inflating the projected spend.

sources.name: tenderly-public-rpc
sources.independence_note: Reads the same chain as thirdweb-public-rpc and passes through Zapproof's own decoder. Agreement between the two is a self-comparison, which prompt Section 6 forbids as a substitute for a cross-check. Admits infrastructure faults only.
sources.free_tier_notes: No account needed. Documented cap of 1 GB per IP per day of response bytes; it counts bytes returned, not requests.
sources.rate_limit: 50 consecutive 1,000-block eth_getLogs calls completed with zero errors at about 2.0 s each, unpaced. A 25-call JSON-RPC batch is rejected with HTTP 429.
sources.terms: Terms of Service contain a 'Prohibited Uses' list; at least one item reads '(xii) attempt to gain unauthorized access to the Tenderly Platform'. The full list was NOT read. Whether bulk read-only eth_getLogs against the public endpoint falls under any prohibited item is UNRESOLVED.
sources.terms_status: OWNER ACCEPTED 2026-10-23 — the owner was shown the partial reading and the quoted Prohibited Uses item, and decided that read-only bulk use of the public endpoint is fair use and not a violation. The owner's judgement, not a formal legal opinion; Phase D's legal signoff still applies.

terms_decision.scope: the whole source-probe terms question was decided in one go, on the same basis as Thirdweb
terms_decision.caveat: A judgement, not a legal review. Phase D's D_LEGAL_SIGNOFF still applies.

sources.verification: used for the 7-day token census (633,877 events) and for eth_call verification of USDC, the Permit2 proxy and the FacilitatorRegistry

sources.name: thirdweb-public-rpc
sources.independence_note: Same as tenderly-public-rpc — same chain, same decoder. Not admissible for G0.3.
sources.free_tier_notes: No account needed. No documented byte allowance found.
sources.rate_limit: Accepts JSON-RPC batches of 25 receipt calls (25/25 returned); rejects a batch of 100 with HTTP 413. Measured 29.4 ms per receipt batched versus 475.1 ms unbatched over the same window.
sources.terms: Terms of Service state: 'You agree not to scrape any content from the Software or use any automated means to access, download or gather information from the Software other than such automated means which may be intentionally made available by the Company'. A public JSON-RPC endpoint is arguably an automated means intentionally made available, but that is an interpretation and not a certainty.
sources.terms_status: OWNER ACCEPTED 2026-10-23 — the owner was shown the quoted restriction and decided that bulk read-only RPC use falls within the 'automated means intentionally made available' carve-out, and that it is good use and lawful. This is the owner's judgement, not a formal legal opinion; prompt Phase D still requires legal signoff before public release.

terms_decision.owner_stated_reason: good use and does not violate the law
terms_decision.caveat: A judgement, not a legal review. Phase D's D_LEGAL_SIGNOFF still applies.

sources.verification: used for the backfill projection's batched receipt measurements

sources.name: substreams-x402-base-pulse
sources.unusable_reason: Does not complete. map_x402_settlements depends on store_facilitator_registry, which Substreams must compute from block 22,666,000 before any settlement can be read — 21,900,000 blocks of preparation. Four attempts (25 min, 40 min, about 1 h, and a full 4 h) produced no settlement data; the best cache accumulation observed was 770,000 blocks in about 4 hours. See reports/failure_analysis_g0_3.md.
sources.independence_note: A third-party Rust/WASM decoder with its own gating logic, so it IS a genuinely independent decode and the only zero-cost candidate found. Marked unusable because it does not complete, not because it is not independent.
sources.auth_required: JWT or API key from thegraph.market. Verified working with the owner's key on 2026-10-16: authentication succeeds and the stream connects. It then fails on store-preparation time, not on auth.
sources.free_tier_notes: thegraph.market free tier: '7M blocks and 5 GiB egress included, no credit card required'. Store preparation alone needs 21.9M blocks, about 3.1x the entire monthly allowance.
sources.rate_limit: 2 concurrent streams. Killed runs hold their session server-side for a while, so attempts interfere.
sources.terms: OWNER ACCEPTED 2026-10-23 as fair use. Not individually reviewed; used only to evaluate feasibility.
sources.terms_status: OWNER ACCEPTED 2026-10-23 — not individually reviewed; the owner decided the whole terms question as fair use on the same basis as Thirdweb. Evaluated as a feasibility test only.

terms_decision.caveat: A judgement, not a legal review. Phase D's D_LEGAL_SIGNOFF still applies.

sources.verification: authentication and streaming verified; map_facilitator_registry_events streamed 100 blocks in 3 s. map_x402_settlements never completed.

eliminated.name: x402scan-api
eliminated.reason: Paid per request. Endpoints return HTTP 402 with a decoded requirement of 10,000 USDC base units, i.e. $0.01 per request, payable in USDC. Any non-trivial cross-check would spend real money and need a funded wallet, violating both the zero-cost cap and the read-only rule.

eliminated.name: base-org-public-rpc

eliminated.name: blockscout-base
eliminated.reason: base.blockscout.com returns HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare challenge ('Just a moment...') on every endpoint tried, with and without a browser user-agent. Confirmed twice: by the independent reviewer on 2026-10-17 and by the agent on 2026-10-23. Blockscout's Ethereum instance (eth.blockscout.com) answers HTTP 200, so the block is specific to how the Base instance is fronted, not a general outage.
eliminated.measured_by: independent reviewer 2026-10-17; re-confirmed by the agent 2026-10-23
eliminated.note: The agent's own task 0.3 probe never tried this source. Independent review pointed out the elimination table was therefore incomplete. Recorded here so the negative is supported by a measurement rather than by omission.

eliminated.name: etherscan-v2-basescan
eliminated.reason: Base mainnet is PAID TIER ONLY on Etherscan V2. Measured directly against the API on 2026-10-23 without needing a valid key, because the tier check runs before the key check: chainid=8453 returns 'Free API access is not supported for this chain. Please upgrade your api plan for full chain coverage.' Controls: chainid=1 returns 'Invalid API Key (#err2)' (supported, key just needed), and chainid=10 returns the same paid-tier message, matching its published status. chainid=84532 (Base Sepolia) returns 'Invalid API Key', so testnet is free but carries no real settlements.
eliminated.unit_cost_if_used: Lite plan — 25% of the previous lowest paid tier; amount not stated publicly
eliminated.note: The owner supplied an ETHERSCAN_API_KEY on 2026-10-23 in good faith after this was raised as the cheapest remaining lead. It cannot be used for Base on the free tier. The key is harmless to keep; it is simply not a path to G0.3.
